source.section: Form 2 PDF p1 lines 1-8 and PDF p2 worksheet lines 1-13; Instructions PDF p12-13 lines 1-8; PDF p17 tax calculation; PDF p18 rate tables; Hub 'Montana Taxable Income Calculation'; Form 2 PDF p3 lines 8-24 print no Social Security subtraction; record social_security; Instructions PDF p13 Line 6, $5,660 subtraction for taxpayers 65 and older; Form 2 PDF p1 line 6; record base.deductions age_65_subtraction

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = private pension (person 0) 30,000.00 + taxable Social Security 13,850.00 = 43,850.00. Federal taxable income = 43,850.00 - standard deduction 17,750.00 (15,750.00 + 1 x 2,000.00 for 65 or older) = 26,100.00 (federal senior deduction ignored, although Montana's line 2 would take it). Filing status single, no Montana standard deduction or exemptions. Schedule I Part I: line 7 additions 0.00; line 24 subtractions 0.00. Form 2 page 1: line 1 federal AGI 43,850.00; line 2 Form 1040 lines 12e and 13b 17,750.00; line 3 26,100.00; line 4 0.00; line 5 0.00; line 6 age 65 subtraction 1 x 5,660.00 = 5,660.00; line 7 Montana taxable income 26,100.00 + 0.00 - 0.00 - 5,660.00 = 20,440.00. Page 2 worksheet: line 1 taxable income 20,440.00; no net long-term capital gain, so lines 2-10 are skipped and line 11 is 0.00; line 12 ordinary income tax from the PDF p18 rate table: 4.7% x 20,440.00 = 960.68; line 13 = 960.68, carried to page 1 line 8. Bracket schedule as numbers (the expected figure): 4.7% x 20,440.00 = 960.68. Line 9 nonrefundable credits 0.00; line 10 tax after credits 960.68. Federal taxable Social Security: provisional income 30,000.00 + 50% x 30,000.00 = 45,000.00; 85% x (45,000.00 - 34,000.00) = 9,350.00 + 4,500.00 = 13,850.00, under the limit 85% x 30,000.00 = 25,500.00. Montana taxes it to the extent it is in federal taxable income; no line subtracts it.
